semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {قَدْ سَمِعَ}: «قد» here is for expectation (tawaqquʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the woman who disputed were both expecting that Allah would hear her dispute and complaint and would send down in that something to relieve her. Clear pronunciation of the dāl before the sīn is the reading of the group, except Abū ʿAmr and the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī]. It is reported of al-Kisāʾī that he said: 'Whoever pronounces the dāl clearly before the sīn has a non-Arab tongue and is not an Arab.' This is not to be dwelt on. «في زَوْجِها» means: concerning his affair, namely his zihār (declaring her like his mother's back) against her."
His saying: {وتشتكي إِلَى الله}: two views are possible. The more apparent is that it is conjoined to «تُجادِلُك», so it too is a ṣila. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e., she disputes with you complaining of her condition to Allah; likewise the clause of His saying {والله يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمآ}, though the circumstantial reading is more remote there.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {الذين يُظَاهِرُونَ}: the disagreement about «يُظاهِرون» was already given in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, and likewise about «اللائي», which spares repeating it here. Ubayy read here «يَتَظاهَرُون», and from him also «يَتَظَهَّرُوْن». There are two views on «الذين». One: it is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is His saying {مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ}. The second: it is accusative through «بصير» [in the previous verse], according to Sībawayh's view that faʿīl may operate; Makkī said it. He means that Sībawayh makes the faʿīl, one of the forms of intensiveness, operate; this is a view that has been criticized in Sībawayh's name, because he cited as evidence for its operating the poet's saying:
4238 - Until a weary, languid one, working at a tiring hour, drove her on ... she spent the night restless, and he spent the night unsleeping
and it was answered that «مَوْهِناً» is an adverb of time, and adverbs are operated upon by whiffs of verbs. This question has a place more fitting than here, but the meaning refuses what Makkī said.
The majority read «أمَّهاتِهم» in the accusative according to the pure Ḥijāzī dialect, as in {مَا هذا بَشَراً} [Yūsuf: 31]. ʿĀṣim in one transmission read it nominative according to the Tamīmī dialect, which is in fact the analogical rule since the particle is not specific [to nouns]. ʿAbd Allāh read «بأمَّهاتهم» with the redundant bāʾ, which allows both dialects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The bāʾ is added in the dialect of those who put the accusative." I say: this is Abū ʿAlī's view; he holds that the bāʾ is added only when «ما» is operative, so it is not added in the Tamīmī nor in the Ḥijāzī if some obstacle prevents its operating, as in "mā in Zaydun bi-qāʾimin". This is refuted by the saying of al-Farazdaq, who is a Tamīmī:
4239 - By your life, Maʿn is not one to abandon his right ... nor is Maʿn a postponer, nor one who makes things easy
and by another's saying:
4240 - By your life, Abū Mālik is not ... weak, nor is his strength feeble
for he added it after «ما» followed by «إنْ».
His saying: {مُنكَراً مِّنَ القول وَزُوراً}: two adjectives of an omitted maṣdar, i.e., "an objectionable saying", and zūr, i.e., a lie and a slander; Makkī said so, and there is something to consider in it, for the implied form becomes: "they surely say an objectionable saying of speech", so that His saying «من القول» has no benefit. It is preferable to say: two adjectives of an omitted object understood from the meaning, i.e., "they say something objectionable of speech", so that the adjective gives something other than what the described noun gave.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {والذين يُظَاهِرُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ. His saying «فتحريرُ رقبةٍ» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, i.e., "so upon them [is]"; or an agent of an implied verb, i.e., "so there is required of them the freeing"; or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e., "so what is obligatory upon them is the freeing". On all three implied forms the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the fāʾ entered because the mubtadaʾ contains the sense of a condition.
His saying: {لِمَا قَالُواْ}: there are several views on this lām. First: it is attached to «يعودون». Under this are several meanings. One: those who by habit used to say this saying in the Jāhiliyya, then return to its like in Islam. Two: then they make good what they said, because one who makes good a matter returns to it, and of this is "a rain came back upon what it had spoiled", i.e., it repaired it by amending; the meaning is that making good this saying and remedying it, by his giving expiation, so that their condition returns to what it was before the zihār. Three: that «ما قالوا» means what they forbade themselves by the wording of zihār, treating the saying as the thing spoken about, like what is mentioned at His saying the Exalted {وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ} [Maryam: 80]; the meaning: then they want to return to physical contact. Al-Zamakhsharī said that. I say: this third is the meaning of what is transmitted from Mālik, al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī: "then they return to intercourse", i.e., they return to what they said they would not return to; so if he made zihār then had intercourse, expiation is incumbent on him according to these. Four: «لما قالوا» means: they say it a second time; so if he said "you are to me as my mother's back" once, there is no expiation, because he has not returned to what he said. This is transmitted from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ashajj, Abū Ḥanīfa, Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Farrāʾ among others, and is the view of the Ẓāhirī jurists. Five: the meaning is that he resolves to keep her and does not divorce her after the zihār, until a time passes in which he could have divorced her; this is the "return" to what he said, and it is the view of al-Shāfiʿī and Mālik, and of Abū Ḥanīfa also. He said: the return here is not repetition of the saying, but in the sense of resolve on intercourse.
Makkī said: "The lām is attached to «يعودون», i.e., they return to intercourse with the one about whom zihār was said, who are the wives; so «ما» and the verb are a maṣdar, i.e., 'to what they say', the maṣdar being in the position of an object, like 'this is a dirham, ḍarb al-amīr', i.e., what is struck by the ruler; so the meaning of 'to their saying' is 'to the one spoken about with zihār', i.e., 'to intercourse with her'." I say: this is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's saying in the third view, whose explanation preceded from al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī and Mālik, except that Makkī restricted it to «ما» being a maṣdar particle so that the interpreted maṣdar takes the place of a passive participle.
There is something to consider in it, as that is permitted even if «ما» is not a maṣdar particle, being in the sense of "that which" or an indefinite described noun. Indeed, making it not a maṣdar particle is preferable, because the interpreted maṣdar is secondary to the explicit maṣdar, the explicit being the origin of the interpreted one, and putting a maṣdar in the place of a passive participle is contrary to the origin; so departure from the origin would be required in two things: the interpreted maṣdar,
then its occurring in the position of a passive participle; and what is preserved from their speech is only putting the explicit maṣdar in place of the object, not the interpreted maṣdar; so know it. It should not be said that making it a non-maṣdar requires an implied omitted muḍāf to make the meaning sound, i.e., "they return to intercourse with the one from whom he made zihār", or "a woman from whom he made zihār", or "they return to keeping her", the origin being no omission; for this obligation is shared between us and you, since you too say that an implied muḍāf is necessary, i.e., "they return to intercourse with, or keeping of, the one about whom zihār was said". What indicates the permissibility of «ما» being non-maṣdar in this view is what Abū al-Baqāʾ pointed to, for he said: "It is attached to «يعودون», meaning 'they return to the one about whom it was said.' This is if you make «ما» a maṣdar particle, and you may make it mean 'that which' and an indefinite described noun."
The second: the lām is attached to «تحرير». There is fronting and postponing in the speech. The implied form: "Those who make zihār against their wives, upon them is the freeing of a slave for what they uttered of zihār, then they return to intercourse after that." This is what Makkī and others transmitted from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash. The Shaykh said: "It is nothing, because it spoils the structure of the verse." There is something to consider in it. We do not concede the spoiling of the structure when the meaning indicates the fronting and postponing; but we concede that claiming fronting and postponing is unnecessary, because it is contrary to the origin.
The third: the lām means «إلى». The fourth: it means «في». Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted these two, and they are very weak; even so, it is attached to «يَعُودون». The fifth: it is attached to «يقولون». Makkī said: "Qatāda said: then they return to what they said of prohibition and make it lawful; so on this the lām is attached to «يقولون»." I say: I do not know what Makkī said here, or how he understood its attachment to «يقولون» on Qatāda's interpretation; rather Qatāda's interpretation is explicit that it is attached to «يَعودون», and there is no basis for its attachment to «يقولون».

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {فَصِيَامُ} and «فإِطعامُ} are like His saying {فَتَحْرِيرُ} in the three views mentioned earlier. «مِنْ قبلِ» is attached to the preceding verb or "settling", i.e., "so there is required of him the freeing or fasting", or "upon him is such-and-such", before the two touch each other. The pronoun in «يتماسَّا» is for the one who made zihār and the one against whom it was made, as what precedes indicates them.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ}: several views. One: it is accusative through «عذابٌ مُهينٌ». Two: it is accusative through an implied verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied "they are humiliated" or "they are punished", or "that settles for them on the day He raises them". Al-Zamakhsharī implied «اذْكُرْ» (remember), saying: "to magnify the day". Three: it is accusative through «لهم», al-Zamakhsharī said, i.e., through the settling it contains, as it is a khabar. Four: it is accusative through «أَحْصاه»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. There is unease in it, because the pronoun in «أحْصاه» returns to what they did.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {مَا يَكُونُ مِن نجوى}: «يكونُ» is complete (tāmma, needing no predicate) and «من نَجْوى» is its agent. «مِنْ» is redundant in it. «نجوى» is originally a maṣdar, so it may remain in its origin and be annexed to its agent, i.e., "there is not found any conspiring of three". It may also be with an omitted muḍāf, i.e., "of those having a secret conversation". It may also be applied to the persons conversing secretly, for emphasis. On these last two views «ثلاثة» is genitive in one of two ways: either a badal from the omitted «ذوي», or an adjective of it on the second implied form; or a badal or adjective of «نَجْوَى» on the third implied form.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ثلاثةً» and «خمسةً» in the accusative as a ḥāl. There are two views on its owner. One: it is omitted together with its nominative operator, its implied form being "they converse as three", omitted because «نجوى» indicates it. The second: it is the latent pronoun in «نجوى» if we make it mean the ones conversing; al-Zamakhsharī said so. Makkī said: "In speech the nominative of «ثلاثة» is permitted as a badal from the position of «نَجْوى», because its position is nominative and «مِنْ» is redundant; and if you put «ثلاثة» in the accusative as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun, when you make «نجوى» mean the ones conversing, it is permitted in speech." I say: as for the nominative, as far as I know it was not read, though it is permitted outside the Quran as he said. As for the accusative, you have learned who read it, so it is as though he did not come across it.
His saying: {إِلاَّ هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ}, «إلاَّ هو خامسُهم», {إِلاَّ هُوَ مَعَهُمْ}: all these clauses after «إلاَّ» are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e., none of these things is found except in one of these states; so the exception is an emptied exception (mufarragh) from the general states.
Abū Jaʿfar read «ما تكونُ» with the feminine tāʾ because «النجوى» is feminine. Abū al-Faḍl said: but the masculine is more common in this chapter, as in the majority's reading, because it is predicated of «مِن نجوى», which is a masculine generic noun.
His saying: {وَلاَ أَكْثَرَ}: the majority read it genitive, conjoined to the wording of «نجوى». Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Abū Ḥaywa and Yaʿqūb read «ولا أكثرُ» nominative. There are two views: one, it is conjoined to the position of «نَجْوى», because it is nominative, with «مِنْ» redundant in it. If it is a maṣdar, it is with an omitted muḍāf as above, i.e., "of those having a secret conversation"; if it means the ones conversing, there is no need for that. The second: «أَدْنى» is a mubtadaʾ and {إِلاَّ هُوَ مَعَهُمْ} is its khabar, so «ولا أكثرُ» is conjoined to the mubtadaʾ, and then «ولا أَدْنَى» is of the type of conjunction of clauses, not of single words.
Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb also, and Mujāhid and al-Khalīl, read «ولا أكبرُ» with the single-dotted bāʾ and nominative, as above. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُنْبِهِمْ», from anbaʾa, except that he omitted the hamza and put kasra on the hāʾ; and it has been read likewise but retaining the hamza and with ḍamma on the hāʾ. The majority read it doubled, from nabbaʾa.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {وَيَتَنَاجَوْنَ}: Ḥamza read «يَنْتَجُوْنَ», from intijāʾ, from najwā. The rest read «يتناجَوْن», from tanājī, also from najwā. Abū ʿAlī said: "The forms iftiʿāl and tafāʿul run the same course, and hence they kept the sound form in «izdawajū» and «iʿtawarū» when they were in the sense of «tazāwajū» and «taʿāwanū». And «حتى إِذَا اداركوا» and «ادركوا» [al-Aʿrāf: 38] have come." I say: the consensus on «تناجَيْتُمْ», «فلا تَتَناجوا» and «وتناجَوْا» supports the majority's reading, for these are from tafāʿul and nothing else, except what is transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh that he read «إذا انْتَجَيْتُم فلا تَنْتَجُوا». The Shaykh transmitted from the Kufans and al-Aʿmash «فلا تَنْتَجُوا» like ʿAbd Allāh's reading. The origin of «تَنْتَجُون» is «tantajiyūna» and of «يتناجَوْن» is «yatanājayūna»; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and dropped, so two quiescent letters met and the yāʾ was dropped for their meeting. Or we say: the weak letter was vowelled and what precedes it was open, so it was turned into alif; two quiescent letters met, so the first was dropped and the fatḥa remained indicating the alif.
[And] Abū Ḥaywa read «بالعِدْوان» with kasra on the ʿayn.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The two readings «ليحزنَ», with ḍamma and with fatḥa, were already discussed in Āl ʿImrān. It has also been read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the zāy, as predicated of the relative noun after it, which is then the agent.
And His saying: {وَلَيْسَ بِضَآرِّهِمْ}: the noun of «ليس» may be a pronoun returning to Satan, and it may return to the grief understood from «ليحزنَ»; al-Zamakhsharī said it. The first is preferable because what it returns to is stated explicitly. [And] al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «ومعصيات» as a plural.
His saying: {لَوْلاَ يُعَذِّبُنَا} [al-Mujādila: 8]: this exhortative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ and Abū Bakr, with disagreement from him, read «انشُزوا» with ḍamma on the shīn in both places; the rest read it with kasra. They are two dialects with one meaning. One says nashaza, i.e., rose, yanshizu and yanshuzu, like ʿarasha yaʿrishu and yaʿrushu, and ʿakafa yaʿkifu and yaʿkufu. This root has already been discussed in al-Baqara.
His saying: {فِي المجالس}: ʿĀṣim read «المجالس» as a plural, considering that each of them has a sitting place. The rest read the singular, since what is meant is the sitting place of the Messenger ﷺ, which is better than its being a singular intended as a plural. It has also been read «في المجلَس» with fatḥa on the lām, which is the maṣdar, i.e., make room in your sitting and do not crowd. Al-Ḥasan, Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, ʿĪsā and Qatāda read «تَفاسَحُوا». Al-fusḥa is spaciousness; fasaḥa lahu means he made room for him.
His saying: {والذين أُوتُواْ}: it may be conjoined to «الذين آمنوا», so it is a conjunction of the specific to the general, because those given knowledge are some of the believers among them. It may also be that «والذين أُوْتُوا» is a conjunction of attributes, i.e., the attributes belong to one entity, as if it were said: Allah raises the believers who are scholars. «دَرَجاتٍ» is a second object; its like was already discussed in al-Anʿām. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the speech is complete at His saying «منكم», and «الذين أُوْتُوا» is accusative through an implied verb, i.e., "and He singles out those given knowledge for degrees", or "and raises them in degrees". [Translator's note: the source reads «اللمَ» (a typographical error) where «العلمَ» (knowledge) is clearly meant; translated as "knowledge".]

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُواْ}: there are three views on this «إذْ». One: it is in its normal sense of the past. The meaning: you neglected that in the past, so make it up by establishing prayer; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. Two: it means «إذا», as in His saying {إِذِ الأغلال} [Ghāfir: 71], which has already been discussed. Three: it means the conditional «إنْ», which is close to the previous, though the difference between «إنْ» and «إذا» is well known. It is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr «خَبِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ» with the yāʾ of the third person; the well-known [reading] from him is with the tāʾ of address like the group.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {مَّا هُم مِّنكُمْ وَلاَ مِنْهُمْ}: three views are possible on this clause. One: it is resumptive with no position in i'rab. He reports of them that they are not of the pure believers nor of the pure disbelievers, but rather as in His saying: {مُّذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذلك لاَ إلى هؤلاء وَلاَ إِلَى هؤلاء} [al-Nisāʾ: 143]. So the pronoun in «ما هم» returns to those who turned away, who are the hypocrites, and in «منهم» it returns to the Jews, i.e., the pure disbelievers. The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَوَلَّوا», and the meaning is as before. The third: it is a second adjective of «قوماً», so on this the pronoun in «ما هم» returns to «قوماً», who are the Jews, and the pronoun in «منهم» returns to those who turned away, meaning: the Jews are not of you, O believers, nor of the hypocrites, and even so the hypocrites took them as allies; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. But in it the pronouns clash, for the pronoun in «ويَحْلِفون» returns to those who turned away. On the first two views the pronouns are the same, returning to those who turned away; on the third they differ, as you have learned in its explanation.
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: a circumstantial clause, i.e., they know it is a lie, so their oath is a plunging oath (yamīn ghamūs) for which they have no excuse.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً}: two objects of «اتَّخذوا». The majority read «أَيْمانَهم» with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of yamīn. Al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, as a maṣdar. And His saying {لَّن تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ} was already treated in Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {استحوذ}: it came in its original form, which is eloquent in usage, though irregular by analogy. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, produced it by analogy and read «استحاذ», like istaqāma. This root was given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ at His saying: {أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 141].

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {كَتَبَ الله لأَغْلِبَنَّ}: «كَتَبَ» may run the course of an oath, and so be answered with what an oath is answered with. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is also said that it is the answer of «كَتَبَ» because it means 'said'." This is nothing, because «قال» does not require an answer, so the correct view is what I gave first. It may also be that «لأَغْلِبَنَّ» is the answer of an implied oath, but that is not apparent.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {يُوَآدُّونَ}: it is the second object of «تَجِدُ». It is also possible that [«تجد»] is the one taking a single object, meaning "meet, encounter", in which case «يوادُّون» is a ḥāl or an adjective of «قوماً». The wāw in «ولو كانوا» is circumstantial, and its explanation has been given more than once. He mentioned fathers first because obedience to them is obligatory on their sons, then the sons second because they are closest to the hearts and are their kernels:
4241 - For our children among us ... are our livers walking on the earth
The well-known verses in the Ḥamāsa. He made brothers third because they are the helpers, in the position of the upper arm to the forearm. He said:
4242 - Your brother, your brother! For he who has no brother ... is like one going to battle without arms
and the cousin of a man, know, is his wing ... and can the hawk rise without a wing?
Then he made the clan fourth, because by it one calls for help and on it one relies. He said:
4243 - They do not ask their brother, when he summons them ... in calamities, for what proof he has said
Abū Rajāʾ read «عشيراتِهم» in the plural, as Abū Bakr read it in al-Tawba likewise. The majority read «كَتَبَ» in the active voice, the agent being Allah the Exalted, with «الإِيمانَ» accusative; Abū Ḥaywa, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of al-Mufaḍḍal, read «كُتِبَ» in the passive, with «الإِيمانُ» nominative through it. The pronoun in «منه» refers to Allah the Exalted. It is also said that it returns to faith, because it is a spirit by which the believers live in both abodes.
